newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stonewalls probe as panel calls security boss.
newsitem.headline: HK stonewalls probe as panel calls security boss.

text.p: A panel grilled Hong Kong's security chief on Tuesday over the mystery of the territory's ousted immigration chief, but the government blocked public disclosure of key evidence.

The Legislative Council panel hauled in the British colony's secretary for security, Peter Lai, to answer questions about checks that were made on disgraced Immigration director Laurence Leung before his sudden forced retirement last July.
The government has said reports on an anti-graft probe and police vetting of Leung's personal integrity formed the basis for its decision to remove Leung from his sensitive post.
It accused Leung of failing to disclose his business dealings as required and of violating repayment terms on a loan.

Lai asked for most of Tuesday's hearing to be held behind closed doors on grounds that the evidence being discussed was confidential, and the public interest would suffer if it were disclosed. Most previous sessions have been open.
When Lai and the panelists returned to open session, legislators pressed Lai to answer when asked to go into details about Leung's financial dealings.
"I cannot really answer that question without going into the kind of material which we just examined and which you asked me about in the camera session," Lai said.
"Those materials are only made fully available to this committee as agreed by the chief secretary -- in camera."
A source close to the inquiry said this would intensify speculation that the government was hiding dirty secrets and that Leung's removal was not just because of his business ties.

The government is under intense pressure to reveal details of the case. Having initially said that Leung had quit for personal reasons last July, it changed its story this month and accused Leung of serious lapses in his personal integrity.
The lapses, which did not amount to criminal offences, made him unfit to stay in a job with top-level security implications in the run-up to Chinese rule on July 1 this year.

Lai categorically denied on Tuesday that the government had ever discussed any other misdeeds by Leung except the mentioned business activities and the loan. He emphatically denied newspaper reports that Leung had committed other misdeeds.
Speculation has been rife that Leung was a Chinese spy, which he has denied. Chief Secretary Anson Chan also dismissed this idea last week when she appeared before the hearing.
Chan will be recalled to testify on February 21, panel chairman Ip Kwok-him said on Tuesday.
The committee asked the government to release a video recording of an interview conducted on Leung by the Independent Commission Against Corruption as soon as possible.
The hearing resumes on Wednesday when the government's personnel chief, Lam Woon-kwong, is to be summoned.
